Quick triage notes (ran live traces against request window you attached):

- Observed symptoms: sudden p99 surge + intermittent 502s correlated with long-context completions (~3.5k token contexts) mixed with short requests.
- Root cause hypothesis: concurrency cap + aggressive per-worker KV cache eviction caused request fan-in and queueing on a small subset of nodes. When a long-context request hits, it stalls the worker, evicting hot KV entries and causing subsequent short requests to refill state and queue.
- Telemetry evidence: worker queue length spike ~08:51:09Z, concurrency_reached=true on 42% of requests, backend_retries increased by 4x.

Recommended immediate mitigations (safe, reversible):
1) Route FastCommerce traffic to model-variant: rwd-small-1024 temporarily (trade slightly lower quality for lower latency). Estimated flip time: 2 minutes.
2) Reduce per-customer concurrency cap from 12 -> 6 for FastCommerce for the next 4 hours to reduce queueing.
3) Enable prefix KV caching stabilization (toggle) to reduce eviction on long-context requests.

I attached a small patch/runbook for the routing flip: runbook_reroute_patch.patch (changeset + rollback steps).

I'll stand by to execute these if we have customer sign-off. If we flip routing, we should see p99 drop within two token batches (~5–10 minutes).

— Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

- Impact: p99 completions increased to ~2.6s; intermittent 502s; estimated checkout abandonment ~1.2% during peak hour. Customer: FastCommerce (high-volume ecomm customer, ARR tier: $1.2M/yr).
- Root cause: a combination of concurrency cap triggers and KV cache eviction when long-context requests are interleaved with short requests — caused transient queueing/backpressure on a subset of workers (ENG-5432).
- What we did: routed to rwd-small-1024, reduced per-customer concurrency cap from 12 to 6, enabled prefix caching stabilization. Observed p99 drop to ~430ms within 20 mins.

3) Provide FastCommerce a formal RCA and a 1:1 with our CTO if requested.
